title: Adam Kadmon: the will for a will, created like a language
overview:
Chapter 18 explains the *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon*. The last level of the *ratzon kadum*, the will for the final finished thing, becomes the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*, which is called *Adam d'Beriya* and thought: a new creation, a something that expresses the true nothing.

Rabbi Walters reads *Adam Kadmon* as association. A person's essential will, for a home or to be kind, says nothing yet about a house or a coat. He has to build a self-image and a worldview, a language inside the will, that tells him what he wants; that connection is the *ratzon l'ratzon*. It is created, not essential: business and learning come and go, connections can be strong or weak, and a bribe can make one. The ten *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon* are such hidden associations, the source of the revealed wills of *Atzilus*: G-d decided to reveal Himself as wise, as a creator, as a king. They come from the *Kav*, yet they are only one of the ways the *ratzon kadum* could come out. The *Kav* itself is above all association, knowing everything by knowing itself.

terms.gloss: the preceding will: an essential will for oneself, like the will for a home, not yet for anything outside
the man of Beriya: Adam Kadmon, which at the general level corresponds to thought and to creation
something from nothing: a new thing, a form that expresses the true, simple nothing
a will for a will: the created association that connects an essential will to a particular thing
enclothed: the will once thought has associated it with a particular thing, like a coat
a bribe: it connects the judge's own will to one side, so his mind is no longer objective
a screen: an interface, like a language, that connects a light so it can be given over
the joining of courtyards for Shabbos: what connects people who each have their own whole path
hidden thought: the subconscious association from which the wills of Adam Kadmon come
self-knowledge: since you know yourself, you know what you want; the ratzon kadum, as against Adam Kadmon

sections.title: The Keser of Adam Kadmon: the last level of the primordial will becomes something new
sections.summary: The *Malchus* of the *ratzon kadum*, the will for the final finished thing, becomes the *Keser* of the *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon*. *Adam Kadmon* is called *Adam d'Beriya* and thought, because it is a creation *yesh me'ayin*: a something that expresses the true nothing, the *Or Ein Sof* in the *Kav*.

phrases.he: (יח) והנה בחינת רצון הקדום לעצמו, כל מה שיהיה בהשתלשלות,
שכלול מי' עד בחינת סוף מעשה שעלה ברצון קדום זה,
phrases.en: has the ten *sefiros* of *igulim* until the *sof maaseh*, which is the *ratzon* for the final finished thing

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת אחרונה שבו
הרי מבחינת מלכות שבעליון נעשה כתר לתחתון כו'
phrases.en: from *Malchus* of a higher level becomes the *Keser* of a lower level

blocks.text: Chapter 18 explains the *yosher* (the straight line) of *Adam Kadmon* (lit. primordial man; the first world); chapter 19, its relation to the lights that come out in *Atzilus* (the world of Emanation).

The *ratzon kadum* (the preceding will) is like the will for a home, what you want to get out of the whole *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent): you want it from something outside you, but you are thinking of what you will get, not of the thing. It **has the ten *sefiros* of *igulim* until the *sof maaseh***, the *sefiros* (Divine attributes) of the *igulim* (circles) down to the *sof maaseh* (the end of the deed): **the *ratzon* for the final finished thing**.

**From *Malchus* of a higher level becomes the *Keser* of a lower level**: that is the general rule, so from the *Malchus* (kingship) of the *igulim* comes the *Keser* (crown) of *Adam Kadmon*. In detail there is enclothing at several levels.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת כתר דאדם קדמון,
phrases.en: And this becomes *Keser* of the *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon*.

phrases.he: להיות ידוע דבחינת אדם קדמון נקרא אדם דבריאה דרך כללות,
phrases.en: when you're speaking of the general worlds, *Adam Kadmon* is called the *Adam d'Beriya*

phrases.he: והוא בחינת המחשבה
phrases.en: and that's *machshava*

phrases.he: ועתיק יומין ואריך אנפין דאצילות
phrases.en: the *Keser* of *Atzilus*

phrases.he: נקרא אדם דיצירה,
phrases.en: is called the *Adam d'Yetzira*

phrases.he: וזעיר אנפין ונוקבא אדם דעשיה כו'
phrases.en: *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva* of *Atzilus* is called *Adam d'Asiya*

blocks.text: **And this becomes *Keser* of the *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon*.** **When you're speaking of the general worlds, *Adam Kadmon* is called the *Adam d'Beriya***, the man of *Beriya* (Creation), **and that's *machshava*** (thought), as *Yetzira* (Formation) is speech and *Asiya* (Action) deed. In a person, the general level is his will working out what he wants; the details, how to get it.

The *hishtalshelus* repeats itself over and over, the same things broken into ever more detail. Once you see the big picture, everything corresponds, and yet each thing has a unique aspect to pick out and then find at every stage. This one is like thought.

*Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin* (lit. the Ancient of Days and the long countenance), **the *Keser* of *Atzilus***, **is called the *Adam d'Yetzira***, and *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva* (lit. the small countenance and the female) of *Atzilus*, *Adam d'Asiya*: the last stage of your will, when it becomes particular and moves your body, as an emotional reaction.

phrases.he: וכמו שהבריאה היא התהוות יש מאין ממש כידוע,
phrases.en: And just like a creation is something new, something *yesh me'ayin*, means that it wasn't there, something from nothing

phrases.he: כך גם בחינת כתר דאדם קדמון זה נקרא בריאה יש מאין
phrases.en: So too *Adam Kadmon* is now something new.

phrases.he: האמיתי דאור אין סוף עצמו שבקו
phrases.en: it's a *yesh* coming from the true *ayin*

phrases.he: הנזכר לעיל הנקרא רצון קדום לעצמו כו'.
phrases.en: the *Or Ein Sof* that's in the *Kav* is called the *ratzon kadum* for Himself

blocks.text: **Just like a creation is something new**, *yesh me'ayin* (something from nothing), **so too *Adam Kadmon* is now something new**: it makes the original will into something new, a *yesh* (something) **from the true *ayin*** (nothing), the *Or Ein Sof* (the infinite light) in the *Kav* (the ray of light), which is totally simple.

The revelation of G-d is totally simple, beyond any form. Revealed now in a form, it is a *yesh* that expresses the *ayin*: that is *yesh me'ayin*. And **the *Or Ein Sof* that's in the *Kav* is called the *ratzon kadum* for Himself**.

sections.title: Adam Kadmon is association: the self-image that turns an essential will into a will for a will
sections.summary: The *ratzon kadum* is the source of every *ratzon l'ratzon*, and the *ratzon l'ratzon* is in *Adam Kadmon*. *Adam Kadmon* is like the self-image and worldview a person creates, a language within the will that tells him what he wants; it is the picture of the perfect world and the perfect person, *Moshiach*.

phrases.he: וביאור הדברים ידוע,
phrases.en: so now we're going to explain

phrases.he: להיות מבואר למעלה דרצון קדום הנזכר לעיל הוא הנקרא מקור כל הרצונות
phrases.en: This *ratzon kadum* that we spoke about in the last two chapters is the source for all the *ratzonos* that come out in this *hishtalshelus*.

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת רצון ההיולי
phrases.en: this is like an essential *ratzon*

phrases.he: להיות ממנו נמצא מקור לכל רצון לרצון
phrases.en: the source for every *ratzon l'ratzon*

blocks.text: **So now we're going to explain.** **This *ratzon kadum* that we spoke about in the last two chapters is the source for all the *ratzonos*** (wills) **that come out in this *hishtalshelus***: a *hiyuli* (raw potential) will, **an essential *ratzon***, **the source for every *ratzon l'ratzon*** (a will for a will), which is in *Adam Kadmon*.

*Adam Kadmon* is like the self-image and worldview a person forms, how everything in the world relates to him. His essential will for a home, to feel a certain way, becomes a will for a house, which includes a will to work to pay for it and for all the details, depending on his circumstances, his society and the world he finds himself in. Tying the essential will to the world around him: that is *Adam Kadmon*.

There are two things. There is his goal, like the man sitting in 770 planning his dream, inside himself but abstract. Then he has to look at the world and create an image that fits the will, which is like *Beriya*: the architect asks what he likes, he says he likes to swim, and the architect concludes he wants a swimming pool.
blocks.title: The dreamer in 770 and the architect

blocks.text: So a new will is created, still within the will: it takes on a tangible form. The basic idea of *Adam Kadmon* is association, the idea of thought and *Beriya*. Making a language, you tie a sound or a shape to an idea and express the idea through the word. Here, within the will, you make a language inside yourself, "so that you know what you want."
A baby starts off with a pain in its stomach when it is hungry; it has to learn to tie that to the desire to eat, and then it knows. This first working out of what you want is the roots of the wills.
blocks.title: The hungry baby

blocks.text: Tying an essential will to other wills is a *ratzon l'ratzon*: the desire becomes a desire for something else. Hungry means you want food; food means putting on your shoes and walking to the store; before that, a will to work for the money. How these wills fit together is an understanding you form of how things work in the world around you.

With that understanding, every will is plugged in and becomes tangible. Someone with an inner will to be connected to G-d, or to be *Chassidish*, forms an image of his goal, to be an *oved* (one who serves G-d) or a *maskil* (a person of intellect), and that becomes his life goal.

That is why *Adam Kadmon* is said to be like the seventy years of a person's life: the image of the perfect him and everything around him. His inner desires from the *ratzon kadum*, for fulfillment and tranquility, become a picture of a utopian life in the world he is in.

The *ratzon kadum* is the will for the *sof maaseh*, the *dira b'tachtonim* (a dwelling below). *Adam Kadmon*, in the *nimshal* (what the analogy stands for), is *Moshiach*: in its *chitzoniyus* (outer side) the picture of the perfect world, in its *pnimiyus* (inner side) the perfect person, *Moshiach* himself. He stands for "and I will dwell within them": the real dwelling is a person totally fixed up.

Now that Yud-Tes Kislev is coming: the Alter Rebbe is said to have been a new soul. Almost all souls were included in *Adam HaRishon* and come out of him as details, so they are already somewhat stuck in the world. That is the *mashal* of the men stuck in a pit and the new man thrown down to them: most souls grow up somewhat believing in the world, and even *tzaddikim* (the righteous) are somewhat stuck in the *hishtalshelus*.
blocks.title: Yud-Tes Kislev: the Alter Rebbe, a new soul

blocks.text: A *Moshiach* soul, and there are a few, like Chanoch, Eliyahu and the Alter Rebbe, was higher than *Adam HaRishon*. It comes into the world and is never trapped by tying G-d's will to a certain form: it sees the G-dliness in everything at once, and the inner goal, with everything a means to it, so it never gets stuck and never loses sight of the real *metzius* (existence) of things.
blocks.title: A Moshiach soul is never trapped by a form

sections.title: The example of kindness: the urge at the door, and the coat it is enclothed in
sections.summary: The *yechida*'s desire for kindness first goes out as a *ratzon kadum*: an urge, still for himself, that the crying man at the door should feel good. Only when thought evaluates the situation and associates it with a coat is it enclothed as a *ratzon l'ratzon*, and that is like a new creation.

phrases.he: ויובן זה על דרך דוגמא מבחינת יחידה שבנפש האדם,
phrases.en: this is like the *yechida* of a person's soul, is like the *etzem hanefesh*

phrases.he: כשעצמיות חפץ חסד שבה, שבהתכללות בבחינת היולי
phrases.en: like the inner *chesed* which is included as a *hiyuli*

phrases.he: כולל כל מה שעתיד לחפוץ ברצון של חסד פרטי כו'
phrases.en: which includes every particular *chesed* they're ever going to want to do

blocks.text: Now he explains it by an example: **this is like the *yechida* of a person's soul**, the *etzem hanefesh* (the essence of the soul), with its *chafetz chesed* (the desire for kindness): **like the inner *chesed*** (kindness) **which is included as a *hiyuli***, **which includes every particular *chesed* they're ever going to want to do**.

phrases.he: כאשר בא ונמשך בדרך פרט לדבר א'
phrases.en: when it now comes to a particular *ratzon*

phrases.he: ויוצא מבחינת העצמיות להיות לו רצון עצמי הנעלם שהוא בחינת רצון קדום הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: so first it goes out of his *etzem* as this first *ratzon kadum*, that he has this inner urge to fulfill his desire for kindness, to express kindness

phrases.he: אבל עדיין בלתי מלובש באותו הדבר כלל,
phrases.en: It's not yet *meluvash* in it.

phrases.he: רק שהרצון הוא לעצמו עדיין כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: it's still for himself

blocks.text: **When it now comes to a particular *ratzon***, his will for kindness ends up as a dollar for the poor man, or a coat or shoes for the freezing one. But **first it goes out of his *etzem*** (essence) **as this first *ratzon kadum***: an inner urge to express kindness.

But it is not yet enclothed in anything. He opens the door, sees the man freezing, and his heart goes out to him at once. He wants him to walk away happy, but is not yet thinking of what he is looking for in the world.
blocks.title: The freezing man at the door

blocks.text: Like someone who wants to get a friend a present: asked what, he does not know yet; it is abstract, that the friend be happy. Or the will for a house as it is described here: he wants his friends to praise him, and does not know what house will do it, but the feeling of showing it off is what he is after. So here: he wants the feeling of having done a nice thing.
blocks.title: A present for somebody, a house to show off

blocks.text: **It's not yet *meluvash*** (enclothed) **in it**: not yet a will for what will help this man. He does not know what the problem is; he hears someone crying and his heart goes out. So **it's still for himself**: he wants the pain of hearing him cry to go away, because he feels bad.

phrases.he: אך כאשר מלובש ופועל רצון לרצון בדבר הפרטי הזה,
phrases.en: but then, when it's *meluvash* in it, it effects a *ratzon l'ratzon* for this particular thing

phrases.he: כמו שמתלבש ופועל רצון לרצון בשכל ומחשבה בדבר פרט הזה,
phrases.en: that means that he now associates it in his *machshava*, in his *sechel*, he associates this inner desire with a particular thing, like to give him a coat

phrases.he: הרי התהוות זה הרצון שבשכל ומחשבה
לדבר זה הוא כמו התהוות בריאה חדשה ממקורו
phrases.en: this is like creating a new thing

phrases.he: והוא מפני שבחינת רצון קדום הנזכר לעיל הוא המקור להתהוות הרצון לרצון הזה שבשכל כו',
phrases.en: This is the source for this associated *ratzon* in his *sechel*.

blocks.text: But **when it's *meluvash* in it, it effects a *ratzon l'ratzon* for this particular thing**: **he now associates it in his *machshava*, in his *sechel***, with a particular thing, like giving him a coat. This happens *davka* (specifically) in intellect and thought: he weighs the situation, forms a picture of what will fulfill the will, and then it becomes a will for that.

Now his will is enclothed in that form, and **this is like creating a new thing**: a will for a coat. From the side of the light, the will for the coat was not there; but the ability to find a fitting form is also part of his essential *hiyuli*, so from that side the coat is there. And the *ratzon kadum* **is the source for this associated *ratzon* in his *sechel***.

sections.title: The will for a will is created: it comes and goes, it can be strong or weak, and a bribe can make it
sections.summary: Business and learning come and go because they are only a means to an end, so the connection between the essential will and the particular will is not essential: it is created, like a language, and has priorities. A bribe makes such a connection, and *Adam Kadmon* is the first and most general one, where the first mistake can be made.

phrases.he: ונקרא רצון לרצון זה בריאה
phrases.en: and this new associated *ratzon*, the *ratzon* for the coat or whatever, is called like a created thing, something new

phrases.he: שהרי אנו רואים שלא בכל העתים יהיה לאדם רצון לרצון פרטי,
phrases.en: even if a person has the same essential *ratzon*, it's not always connected to the same *ratzon l'ratzon*

phrases.he: כמו הרצון במסחור או בלימוד
phrases.en: like the desire to do business or to learn

phrases.he: שבהכרח יש מקור המהווה לרצון זה הפרטי
ונקרא רצון לרצון זה,
phrases.en: and this inner *ratzon* is called the *ratzon* for this *ratzon*, the inner desire that was powering and the source of this associated *ratzon*, this secondary *ratzon*

blocks.text: So **this new associated *ratzon*, the *ratzon* for the coat or whatever, is called like a created thing, something new**. For **even if a person has the same essential *ratzon*, it's not always connected to the same *ratzon l'ratzon***, **like the desire to do business or to learn**.

There must be a source that makes this particular will. Nobody always feels like working or studying, since it is a means to an end. He does business to make money, and once he has it the deal no longer interests him; he studies to understand something, and once he knows it he no longer just feels like learning.
blocks.title: Business and learning are a means to an end

blocks.text: **This inner *ratzon* is called the *ratzon* for this *ratzon***: the inner desire that powers the associated will, the business or the learning, and is its source.

phrases.he: וממילא מובן מאחר שלא בכל העתים נמשך הרצון לרצון זה,
phrases.en: since the essential *ratzon* doesn't always come into this associated *ratzon*

phrases.he: וגם לפעמים יאיר אור רב ותקיף
phrases.en: and also sometimes it will shine very strongly, they'll want it very much

phrases.he: ולפעמים יאיר במיעוט וחלישות כו',
נמצא מוכרח שגם המקור העושה ומהוה לרצון זה, הנקרא רצון לרצון, הוא גם כן בא בבחינת התהוות יש מאין
phrases.en: even this association between the two things, which is the source, what connects the one *ratzon* to the other *ratzon*, that is also created

blocks.text: So, **since the essential *ratzon* doesn't always come into this associated *ratzon***, **and also sometimes it will shine very strongly, they'll want it very much**, and sometimes weakly, really into the business or just doing it, the source that makes this will, the *ratzon l'ratzon*, must also come as a creation, *yesh me'ayin*.

If the desire for kindness were essentially tied to the coat, it would always come out. But the desire for money sometimes comes out as business and sometimes not, the wish to know sometimes as learning and sometimes not, because they are not essentially tied: a person can have an inner will and not know what will fulfill it. So **even this association between the two things, which is the source, what connects the one *ratzon* to the other *ratzon*, that is also created**: he has to decide it.

It is like a person's *bittul* (self-nullification), his *mesirus nefesh* (self-sacrifice) to the One whose will it is: it attaches to a particular thing only when He says that is what He wants, and if He wants something else, it does that.

So the connection can change and can have priorities, stronger or weaker. Were the two essentially tied, this would simply equal that, with no main and secondary, no higher and lower. Since the whole thing is created, it could be otherwise, and one thing can be made more connected and another less.

phrases.he: כמו השוחד,
phrases.en: and it's like a bribe

phrases.he: שיעשה רצון לרצון ושכל לזכות תמיד
phrases.en: that a bribe connects his *ratzon* for the money to the *ratzon* for this guy to be innocent

blocks.text: **And it's like a bribe**: **a bribe connects his *ratzon* for the money to the *ratzon* for this guy to be innocent**. His will for money has nothing essentially to do with the verdict, but the man offers the money only on that condition, and now they are tied.

There is no direct connection; it is circumstantial, like making a language. Only this is a language within your will, how you speak to yourself to know what you want; the actual creation of the details is a language for speaking to others, like English or Hebrew. It is the same idea.
No. It is a will, much as we use it, but not an essential desire. *Ratzon kadum* means the essential psychological needs of all people, before anything to do with society or circumstance.
blocks.question: Is the desire for money a *ratzon kadum*?

blocks.text: There you are creating a *yosher*, and *yosher* always means association. It is making a language: you take a number of *masachim* (screens), essential forms, tie one to another, and use them to convey a light. Doing so also creates a hierarchy, main and secondary, which is to think of higher and lower.

It is *mamash* (actually) like a language. Take the word water: you take the thing, water, and that sound, and connect them. So there are three things: water, the sound of the word, and the ability to connect them, to associate.
blocks.title: The word water

blocks.text: That is the *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon*: it makes a *masach* (screen), an interface like a language, that ties a light so it can be given over to someone else. That is the *bekia* (breaking through) of the *masach*: hearing the words, you extract the intellect from them, and the original intellect shines through.

A person's bank of knowledge of the world, the raw facts of his experience, is the material of the *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon*, and the structure built from it is like a body; the *igulim* are like the soul; the way he ties them is the *ratzon l'ratzon*.

So a want in your essence, the *igulim*, a spiritual thing, does not attach by itself to a thing in the world, as your power of intellect is tied to your brain (as will come with the lights and vessels of *Atzilus*). In every world the *igulim* are to the *yosher* as soul to body, lights to vessels.

What is unique in *Adam Kadmon* is that it is the original, general tie of all your wills to the general form; later ones, how you will get it in the circumstances, are more detailed. So it is called the seventy years of a person's life: the most general form a person makes of who he is.

This is the first chance a person has to make a mistake, because here he needs an interpretation. The facts everybody knows: what he wants, and the outside world. A mistake in how the two fit together is the source of a *shevira* (the breaking of the vessels).

A person does this too: from birth he starts forming his self-image and worldview. There is a deeper *hishtalshelus* in the soul itself, but the *mashal* we always use is the one we really understand, the *hishtalshelus* of the vital soul, the animal soul, once the soul is in the body. Until about five a child forms this self-image and worldview; it sets his personality for life and is very hard to change.

blocks.text: The same happens to the G-dly soul before it comes into the body: it is shown the sparks it is to refine, and that gives it a form. The source of the *shevira* there is that each soul sees only its part of the plan, so a separation can come. That is why an *eruv chatzeiros* (the joining of courtyards for Shabbos) is needed to connect many private domains. In his own four cubits all is holiness, Torah and mitzvos; but his way is right for him, and he does not understand that another has a different nature and a different service.

blocks.text: If he cannot understand that and connect the two, there can still be a separation, as the Mitteler Rebbe says in *Derech Chaim*, even between great, holy, whole rabbis; historically there were always fights. The fight between the Chassidim and the Misnagdim started in the time of the Rishonim, over practical Kabbala, then over Kabbala in general, down through the Yaavetz, the Ramchal, Rabbi Yonasan Eybeschutz and the Baal Shem Tov, then the Gra and the Alter Rebbe. The point was that the Misnagdim were Torah souls and the Chassidim more *tefilla* (prayer) souls, as the Alter Rebbe told the government when it interrogated him. But the Misnagdim thought that not putting the emphasis on Torah was like heresy.
blocks.title: Chassidim and Misnagdim: Torah souls and tefilla souls

sensitivity.reason: Tells the history of the dispute between Chassidim and Misnagdim loosely and from memory, and says the Misnagdim thought the Chassidim's lack of emphasis on Torah was like heresy.
sensitivity.publishable: If he cannot understand that and connect the two, there can still be a separation, as the Mitteler Rebbe says in *Derech Chaim*, even between great, holy, whole rabbis; historically there were always fights. In the dispute between the Chassidim and the Misnagdim, the point was that the Misnagdim were Torah souls and the Chassidim more *tefilla* (prayer) souls, as the Alter Rebbe told the government when it interrogated him.

blocks.text: Other things were involved too: it got ugly as people got personally involved and became a whole *kelipa* (what conceals G-dliness), but its source was in holiness. Such a difference is the root: each has his own path in serving G-d and does not see it all serve one intention, and once it came down to people less holy, it led to complete separation, *mamash* baseless hatred, people actually killing each other and making accusations. So the source of this separation is already in the G-dly soul, in which part of *Adam Kadmon* it comes from.

sensitivity.reason: Says the dispute between Chassidim and Misnagdim led to people actually killing each other, a charge against both groups stated as history.
sensitivity.publishable: Other things were involved too: it got ugly as people got personally involved and became a whole *kelipa* (what conceals G-dliness), but its source was in holiness. Such a difference is the root: each has his own path in serving G-d and does not see it all serve one intention, and once it came down to people less holy, it led to complete separation, *mamash* baseless hatred, people making accusations against each other. So the source of this separation is already in the G-dly soul, in which part of *Adam Kadmon* it comes from.

blocks.text: That is why you need *davka* a leader. A Rebbe, the head of the Jewish people, is a general soul who sees the whole picture, each person's service a detail of the whole. So he can tell each what to do and how to work together, and unite everybody, up to the general soul of all the generations, *Moshiach* himself.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 64 opens by carrying on the end of class 63 (on Adam Kadmon, self-image and the source of the shevira) and reads line 16 again only at w1724; placed under line 16, the passage class 63 stopped on.

blocks.text: On the side of the vital soul, someone growing up in a *goyishe* world easily gets wrong ideas. Even in holiness: if the people around him take what is right for them as the only right way, he can think he has to be like them, which is not best for his own service. He tries, it does not work, and he is disillusioned. Unless he sees there is something deeper, not bound to that form, and finds the right role model, service and self-image, "then big problems."
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 64 opens by carrying on the end of class 63 (on Adam Kadmon, self-image and the source of the shevira) and reads line 16 again only at w1724; placed under line 16, the passage class 63 stopped on.

sensitivity.reason: Calls the non-Jewish world "a goyishe world", a Yiddish word that reads as contemptuous in print.
sensitivity.publishable: On the side of the vital soul, someone growing up in a non-Jewish world easily gets wrong ideas. Even in holiness: if the people around him take what is right for them as the only right way, he can think he has to be like them, which is not best for his own service. He tries, it does not work, and he is disillusioned. Unless he sees there is something deeper, not bound to that form, and finds the right role model, service and self-image, "then big problems."

blocks.text: This is a problem on the side of *kelipa* and of holiness alike. Teenagers struggle with it when they start trying to live up to the self-image they had: they are trying to find themselves, how they fit into the picture and can actually be that.

blocks.text: That is why stories matter. Stories of *tzaddikim* and Chassidim, of great people who embody the thing, give the image of the real final goal: how to bring the Torah down into life. Everyone can learn from every story, but each has a type of hero he identifies with and tries to be like, certain stories that really inspire him, and he lives by their message.

blocks.text: The whole purpose of the *maamarim* (discourses) is to understand what was going on in the story and how you can actually be like that, so that it does not become copying the outward symptoms. Dressing like someone is easy; everyone does it with role models, sports stars, movie stars, getting the paraphernalia, and Chassidim also copy people. They see who they want to be and copy it, but without catching the real thing behind it, it will not get them there.

blocks.text: Here, though, the will for the *dira b'tachtonim* became a will for a certain form. *Adam Kadmon* is the source of the Torah and mitzvos, and of the form of the world we live in. That is the *chitzoniyus*: which world will be the dwelling, which lower place we will have. The Torah and mitzvos are the *pnimiyus*, the will for how to make that lower place a dwelling. So too the souls of Israel: how they will be, the souls becoming like created beings, happens in *Adam Kadmon*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 64 opens by carrying on the end of class 63 (on Adam Kadmon, self-image and the source of the shevira) and reads line 16 again only at w1724; placed under line 16, the passage class 63 stopped on.

blocks.text: Until then the soul is a part of G-d, not something separate. What is created is *davka* the form the soul takes on, not its essence. So everyone's form, the root of his soul and his mission, is rooted in *Adam Kadmon*.

blocks.text: Like the bribe: once money is tied to his essential will, he has a personal interest. His will for himself, already tied to money from before, binds his intellect, and it is no longer objective. He sat as judge because his interest was justice; now he wants something for himself, and that bends his will for justice to fit his will for money, so he will always have a will for merit.

phrases.he: מפני שהשוחד מגיע בעצמות נפשו,
phrases.en: because the *shochad* connects his *etzem* to it

phrases.he: שמחמתו יומשך תמיד התהוות רצון לרצון של חסד וזכות
phrases.en: This will always cause that he'll have a bias now for *chesed* and for merit.

phrases.he: ולהיפך לשונאו
phrases.en: for his enemy

phrases.he: יתהווה תמיד רצון לרצון של דין כו' וכהאי גוונא ודי למבין.
phrases.en: And for somebody that he hates, since he has a personal interest against the person, he'll always look to find him guilty and look negatively on him.

blocks.text: **Because the *shochad* connects his *etzem* to it**: the *shochad* (a bribe) reaches the essence of his soul, so it **will always cause that he'll have a bias now for *chesed* and for merit**. And the reverse **for his enemy**: with a personal interest against him, he will always look to find him guilty.

sections.title: Ten wills for a will: Adam Kadmon as the hidden source of the wills of Atzilus
sections.summary: Every revealed will has ten, so a person makes ten associations, a whole self-image; a Jew's real self-image is to do whatever is needed. So too the ten *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon* are only *ratzon l'ratzon*, the hidden source of the revealed *sefiros* of *Atzilus*: G-d decided to reveal Himself as wise and as a creator.

phrases.he: וידוע דכל רצון גלוי כלול מי'.
phrases.en: every revealed *ratzon* has ten *sefiros*

phrases.he: אם כן גם הרצון לרצון זה כלול מי'
phrases.en: it must also have ten

phrases.he: ויש י' כחות, ממילא יש י' מיני רצון לרצון,
phrases.en: There's ten, you have to make ten associations

phrases.he: שמתהווים כולם בבחינת יש מאין כו'
phrases.en: it creates each of these *ratzonos* in a way of *yesh me'ayin*, that it creates from the abstract *ratzon* the concrete thing

blocks.text: **Every revealed *ratzon* has ten *sefiros***, so the will for a will **must also have ten**: to know how to move the intellect and the emotions, you need an image tying the essential will, with its hidden ten, to each. A child's will for a home is a feeling, and it has a say in every room: the kitchen, the dining room, the living room.

There are ten powers, so **there's ten, you have to make ten associations**: how a person sees his intellect, his *chachma* (wisdom) and *bina* (understanding), his *chesed*, everything. A whole self-image, himself in the classroom and on the sports field, what he wants of each and how it fits together. So different people make different wills.

Some people form a self-image like the saying of the Rebbe Rashab. A *maskil* is one who learns all day, an *oved* one who *davens* all day; who is an *oved* and a *maskil*? "The one that peels potatoes for the *farbrengen*" (a Chassidic gathering). A self-image wholly in one thing shuts out everything else: the *maskil* has no time to *daven*, the *oved* none to learn. But one whose will is to do whatever G-d wants does what is needed now: time to learn, he learns; time to *daven*, he *davens*; potatoes for the *farbrengen*, he peels them.
blocks.title: Who is a maskil and an oved? The one who peels potatoes

blocks.text: That is what a Jew is: his real inner will, his real self-image, is to be able to do anything, to be flexible, doing *davka* whatever needs to be done.
And the *goyim* (the nations) are each set in a certain order, a will to be like this and like that, and that is their thing. That is why each one has its *mazal* (a ruling star).

sensitivity.reason: Speaks of "the goyim" as all set in their ways ("that's their thing"), against the Jew's flexibility; the teaching behind it is the mazal of each nation.
sensitivity.publishable: And the nations are each set in a certain order, a will to be like this and like that. That is why each one has its *mazal* (a ruling star).

blocks.text: The will for a will **creates each of these *ratzonos* in a way of *yesh me'ayin***: it **creates from the abstract *ratzon* the concrete thing**, the something out of the nothing, by associating them.

phrases.he: וכל זה דוגמא להבין בבחינת עשר ספירות דאדם קדמון, שכללותם ענין רצון לרצון לבד
phrases.en: The whole *inyan* of *Adam Kadmon* is the association of a *ratzon* to another *ratzon*.

phrases.he: שהרי הן בחינת ההעלם דעשר ספירות דאצילות שבגלוי כידוע
phrases.en: the *Adam Kadmon* is the *helem* for the *sefiros* of *Atzilus*

blocks.text: This is an example for the ten *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon*: **the whole *inyan* of *Adam Kadmon* is the association of a *ratzon* to another *ratzon*** (*inyan*: matter), and **the *Adam Kadmon* is the *helem* for the *sefiros* of *Atzilus*** (*helem*: concealment): their revealed wills seek to fulfill the form made in *Adam Kadmon* from the *ratzon kadum*.

phrases.he: וכמו כתר דחכמה דאצילות
phrases.en: the *ratzon* for *chachma* of *Atzilus*, which is like the *ratzon* for the *chachma* of the Torah

phrases.he: שהוא הרצון שבשכל כו'
phrases.en: that *Hashem* has a *ratzon* to make the Torah be the most amazing book ever

phrases.he: שרשו בכתר שבחכמה דאדם קדמון
phrases.en: the source of that is in the *Keser sheb'chachma* of *Adam Kadmon*

phrases.he: שנקרא רצון לרצון זה
phrases.en: which is called the *ratzon* for this *ratzon*

phrases.he: וכן כתר שבחסד דאצילות
phrases.en: the *ratzon* for *chesed* of *Atzilus*, which is the *ratzon* to create this world

phrases.he: מכתר שבחסד דאדם קדמון כו'
phrases.en: Which is like the *Keser* *chesed* of *Adam Kadmon*.

blocks.text: Like **the *ratzon* for *chachma* of *Atzilus*, which is like the *ratzon* for the *chachma* of the Torah**: **that *Hashem* has a *ratzon* to make the Torah be the most amazing book ever**, and to show the wisdom in creation too. That will comes from *Adam Kadmon*, the way G-d wants to reveal Himself.

He decided to reveal Himself as wise. From G-d's side, He chose to tie Himself to the form of *Adam Kadmon*, "the G-d form", the highest form we have. Revealing Himself as the *chachma* of *Adam Kadmon*, the G-d of intellect, makes a will to reveal wisdom in the world, and **the source of that is in the *Keser sheb'chachma* of *Adam Kadmon***, **which is called the *ratzon* for this *ratzon***.

So too **the *ratzon* for *chesed* of *Atzilus*, which is the *ratzon* to create this world**, a particular thing, comes from the will to reveal Himself as a creator: **the *Keser* *chesed* of *Adam Kadmon***. *Adam Kadmon* ties His essential will, the real *ratzon kadum*, to how He will reveal Himself: first the picture of what He will reveal, then from it how to reveal it in the world.

sections.title: From the Kav: only one of the ways the primordial will could come out, and all of it hidden
sections.summary: The ten *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon* come from the *Kav*, the essential will, which chose this form as a vessel and makes a will for every detail, from *Keser* to *Malchus*. But *Adam Kadmon* is only the outer side of the *ratzon kadum*, one way out of many, and it is all hidden: a subconscious association, like a language learned before one speaks.

phrases.he: ואמנם התהוות עשר ספירות דאדם קדמון עצמו,
phrases.en: but where did these *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon* come from?

phrases.he: הכל נמשך מבחינת הקו שנקרא מקור התהוות כל הרצונות לרצונות כו'
phrases.en: These are all from the *Kav*

phrases.he: להיותו עצם הרצון הפשוט שקדם בעצמו שיהיה כך כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: they all come from the *ratzon kadum*, which is the *etzem ratzon*

blocks.text: **Where did these *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon* come from?** **These are all from the *Kav***. G-d picks this form the way a teacher plans how the intellect will come out, with a hierarchy, a beginning and a next level. Since He chose this form as the vessel for the light, it too reveals His essence.
The *Kav* is called the source of all the wills, and **they all come from the *ratzon kadum*, which is the *etzem ratzon***, the essential will; all these are only a vessel to serve it.

phrases.he: על כן הוא פועל ועושה רצון לרצון בדרך פרט
phrases.en: Therefore, since this *etzem ratzon* also comes in to create a *ratzon* for every *prat*

phrases.he: והוא מבחינת כתר דאדם קדמון עד בחינת מלכות שבו,
phrases.en: the whole *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon* from *Keser* to *Malchus*

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת רצון לרצון דמלוכה כו'
phrases.en: which *Malchus* is the *ratzon l'ratzon* for *melucha*

blocks.text: **Therefore, since this *etzem ratzon* also comes in to create a *ratzon* for every *prat*** (detail), as with the house, it is enclothed in each detail, for how that detail fits the essential will.

These are **the whole *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon* from *Keser* to *Malchus***. *Malchus* **is the *ratzon l'ratzon* for *melucha*** (kingship): G-d wants to reveal Himself as king, which makes a will for separate beings who feel free to do as they like and listen to G-d only because they must, because He is the king.

phrases.he: ואמנם רק מבחינת אחרונה שברצון הקדום ההיולי הנזכר לעיל נעשה בחינת כתר דאדם קדמון
phrases.en: but *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon* is only from the *chitzoniyus* of the *ratzon kadum*

blocks.text: But the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon* is **only from the *chitzoniyus* of the *ratzon kadum***: only one way it could be expressed, not its essence. *Adam Kadmon* does not grasp the full *ratzon kadum*, which could come out another way.

Take someone who wants to be the rich man with the big house. In America that is a brick mansion, a nice lawn and a Cadillac; in another society, let's say in Africa, two huts and a couple of cows. It also depends on the place: in Israel houses are stone, to stay cool in the heat with little wood; in America, insulated against the cold. So *Adam Kadmon* is only one little way the essential will could come out, of many.
blocks.title: A mansion, two huts, a stone house

sensitivity.reason: Uses a stock picture of Africa (a hut, two huts and a couple of cows) as the contrast to an American mansion.
sensitivity.publishable: Take someone who wants to be the rich man with the big house. In America that is a brick mansion, a nice lawn and a Cadillac; in another society, two huts and a couple of cows. It also depends on the place: in Israel houses are stone, to stay cool in the heat with little wood; in America, insulated against the cold. So *Adam Kadmon* is only one little way the essential will could come out, of many.

phrases.he: שהוא רצון לרצון הנעלם שלמעלה מחכמה שברצון לרצון הנעלם כו'
phrases.en: the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon* is the *ratzon* to create this form, the associations, which is higher than the *chachma* of *Adam Kadmon*

phrases.he: ועל דרך זה כל עשר ספירות דאדם קדמון, הכל בבחינת ההעלם
phrases.en: It's all *b'helem*, meaning that it's all like a subconscious thing

phrases.he: ורצון לרצון לכל עשר ספירות דאצילות שבא בבחינת גלוי,
כמו שיתבאר ודי למבין:
phrases.en: we'll explain the next *perek* how the *ratzonos* of *Atzilus* come out from *Adam Kadmon*

blocks.text: Only from the *chitzoniyus* of the *ratzon kadum* does it become the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*, the hidden will for a will: **the *ratzon* to create this form, the associations, which is higher than the *chachma* of *Adam Kadmon***.

So all ten *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon*: **it's all *b'helem*** (hidden), **meaning that it's all like a subconscious thing**, not yet an actual will. Like knowing a language: you are not saying anything yet, you just know which word to use for this. *Adam Kadmon* only makes the association: when you want a house, this is the house you want.
You form that as a little child, but do not want the house until you are twenty-five or so. The will for the will was set up already, only hidden, a subconscious association.

Or commercials: they set it up so you tie your essential will, being thirsty, to Coca-Cola, and when you are thirsty you buy their drink. The inner connection is subconscious; that is why it is called a hidden will.
blocks.title: Thirsty, so Coca-Cola

blocks.text: As for the revealed will for a will of the *sefiros* of *Atzilus*: **we'll explain the next *perek*** (chapter) **how the *ratzonos* of *Atzilus* come out from *Adam Kadmon***.

sections.title: Why Adam Kadmon is called Beriya and thought, and the Kav that is above it
sections.summary: *Adam Kadmon* is the man of *Beriya* because the will for a will is created according to circumstances, and it starts in thought: the will associated with a picture. Its *Keser*, *chachma* and *bina* make the associations in a hidden thought. The *Kav* is higher: an essential will that knows everything by knowing itself, as the Rambam says.

phrases.he: וזהו שבחינת אדם קדמון נקרא אדם דבריאה כו',
phrases.en: this is why *Adam Kadmon* is called the man of *Beriya*, the creation

phrases.he: כמו בחינת התהוות יש מאין
phrases.en: it's creating something from nothing

phrases.he: כנראה בחוש שהתהוות הרצון לרצון לעתים מיוחדים הוא בא, כשאר התהוות איזה מציאות כו'
phrases.en: that the *ratzon haratzon* is created according to the circumstances, like any other *metzius* that's not an essential thing

blocks.text: And **this is why *Adam Kadmon* is called the man of *Beriya*, the creation**: **it's creating something from nothing**. The will for a will **is created according to the circumstances, like any other *metzius* that's not an essential thing**.

phrases.he: והוא כמו התהוות המחשבה,
phrases.en: It's like creation of a *machshava*

phrases.he: שהיא התהוות יש מאין לגבי עצמיות הרצון שבנפשו
phrases.en: like when you make a language, that you associate your *etzem haratzon* with a certain thought

phrases.he: כנראה בחוש שהרצון לרצון הבא בבחינת התהוות כנזכר לעיל,
תחלת התהוותו במחשבה דוקא
phrases.en: and this is first done in *machshava*, that you associate your *etzem haratzon* with a certain form, a certain picture

phrases.he: כי המחשבה בחינת כלי לרצון,
phrases.en: the *machshava* is a *kli* for the *ratzon*

phrases.he: שהרצון מתלבש במחשבה,
phrases.en: that your *ratzon* becomes associated with a certain picture, a certain thought

phrases.he: כמו וחשב לעשות כו'
phrases.en: like it says, he thought to do

phrases.he: וכן תחלת התהוות רצון לרצון במחשבה,
phrases.en: and so too the beginning of the *ratzon haratzon* also is in *machshava*

phrases.he: הוא שנקרא רצון שבמחשבה כו'
phrases.en: this is called the *ratzon* within the *machshava*

blocks.text: **It's like creation of a *machshava***, a thought: **like when you make a language, that you associate your *etzem haratzon* with a certain thought**, so that wanting something, you picture a certain thing. The will for a will comes about that way, **and this is first done in *machshava*, that you associate your *etzem haratzon* with a certain form, a certain picture**.

For **the *machshava* is a *kli* for the *ratzon***, a *kli* (vessel): **your *ratzon* becomes associated with a certain picture, a certain thought**, **like it says, he thought to do**. **So too the beginning of the *ratzon haratzon* also is in *machshava***, which is why *Adam Kadmon* is called thought, and **this is called the *ratzon* within the *machshava***.

phrases.he: וזהו כללות ענין כח''ב דאדם קדמון
phrases.en: the *inyan* of the *Keser*, *chachma*, *bina* of *Adam Kadmon*

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת התהוות פעולת אור רצון לרצון דרך פרט
phrases.en: the *KaChaB* of *Adam Kadmon* is what creates the association

phrases.he: שבא במחשבה סתימאה כו'
phrases.en: which come out from the *machshava stima'a*

blocks.text: This is **the *inyan* of the *Keser*, *chachma*, *bina* of *Adam Kadmon***: **the *KaChaB* of *Adam Kadmon* is what creates the association**, and its *middos* (emotional attributes) are the effect, wanting this and not that. They **come out from the *machshava stima'a***, the hidden thought: a subconscious association, hence *stima'a*.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן בבחינת הקו עצמו שלמעלה מבחינת פעולת התהוות רצון לרצון לדבר פרט במחשבה סתימאה גם כן כו'
phrases.en: but the *Kav* was higher than being associated even in *machshava stima'a* with any sort of a *ratzon*

phrases.he: רק לעצמו עדיין
phrases.en: It's just an essential desire for you to feel a certain way, not connected to any picture or something outside.

phrases.he: חושב כל מה שיהיה כו'
phrases.en: you just think of everything that will be, in an abstract, in an essential way

phrases.he: שכולל במחשבת עצמו עדיין
phrases.en: and it's so included in his own *machshava*

phrases.he: ולא בהתהוות רצון במחשבה שחוץ ממנו כלל ודי למבין
phrases.en: and not in a creation or association of something outside of him at all

phrases.he: (ובלשון הרמב''ם היינו בידיעת עצמו ולא בידיעה שחוץ ממנו וכו' וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר):

blocks.text: But **the *Kav* was higher than being associated even in *machshava stima'a* with any sort of a *ratzon***. **It's just an essential desire for you to feel a certain way, not connected to any picture or something outside**: **you just think of everything that will be, in an abstract, in an essential way**.

It is **so included in his own *machshava***, **and not in a creation or association of something outside of him at all**: in the Rambam's words, by knowing Himself, not by a knowledge outside Him. That is *yedias atzmo* (self-knowledge): knowing yourself, you know what you want. That is the *ratzon kadum*; *Adam Kadmon* is already a knowledge outside Him.

reviewQuestions.question: Why is the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon* called a creation *yesh me'ayin*, and what is the true *ayin* it comes from?
In the example of the man at the door, what is still *ratzon kadum* and what has become a *ratzon l'ratzon*?
How does the fact that a person does not always want to do business or to learn show that the *ratzon l'ratzon* is created?
What does a bribe do to a judge, and why does it make him look for merit, or for guilt in his enemy?
Why is the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon* only from the outer side of the *ratzon kadum*, and what do the houses in different countries show?
How is the *Kav* different from the *Keser*, *chachma* and *bina* of *Adam Kadmon*, and what do the Rambam's words about knowing Himself add?

notes.text: The machine hears ratzon l'ratzon as "ratzon v'ratzon" in classes 62 and 63 and as "ratzon sheb'ratzon" or "ratzon haratzon" in class 65. The prose writes *ratzon l'ratzon* throughout; the phrase of line 7 (62 w757-762, heard "ratzon v'ratzon") is written *ratzon l'ratzon*, and the phrases of lines 35, 39 keep *ratzon haratzon* as heard.

63 w1654-1707 ("No, that's a ratzon... not actually a ratzon kadum") answers a question that is not on the tape. Written as a question block with askedBy student and the question inferred from the answer ("Is the desire for money a ratzon kadum?"). A reviewer should listen.

Class 64 opens (w0-1723) carrying on the end of class 63 about Adam Kadmon, the self-image and the source of the shevira (the soul's descent, Chassidim and Misnagdim, the leader, role models, stories), before rereading line 16. All of it is placed under line 16 with outOfPlace.

The history of the Chassidim and Misnagdim (64 w366-606) is as he gives it: that it began in the time of the Rishonim over practical Kabbala, then through the Yaavetz, the Ramchal, Rabbi Yonasan Eybeschutz, the Baal Shem Tov, the Gra and the Alter Rebbe; and the Alter Rebbe's answer under interrogation. *Derech Chaim* is cited as he cites it. A reviewer may want to check the history. He joins into one process controversies usually told apart (the Yaavetz and Rabbi Yonasan Eybeschutz disputed over amulets, before the Chassidim and Misnagdim), and the killing at 64 w725 is his word; both are left as he says them, and the public version leaves out the history, the heresy remark and the killing.

Phrases he reads without translating keep their Hebrew alone: the start and end of line 1, the middle of line 11 ("harei hishavus zeh haratzon sheb'sechel u'machshava"), the first half of line 14, the weak half of line 15 (his gloss there is about business, not a rendering), the first half of line 33, the first half of line 37, and line 44 (at 65 w2352-2371 he explains it rather than translating it). The English of line 27 (65 w1123-1137) and of line 28 (w1163-1181) is his explanation right after he reads them.
The line 3 mark (62 w204) falls mid-sentence on the line 2 explanation; he reads line 3 at w246. The first phrase of line 3 cites w237-245, said just before the reading.
"It says" that Adam Kadmon is like the seventy years of a person's life, and that Adam Kadmon is Moshiach (62 w1540-1682, 63 w2260-2291): he gives no source; kept as he says it.

Sensitivity, since Rabbi Walters has allowed a public edition: the flags on 64 w366-606, w607-791, w896-1091 and 65 w480-518, w1361-1545 replace only the history and the heresy remark, the killing, the word goyishe, the goyim remark (kept as the mazal of each nation, an ordinary Torah position) and Africa. Left unflagged as Torah positions: the Alter Rebbe as a Moshiach soul higher than Adam HaRishon, a Rebbe as a general soul, Chassidim copying people's dress.
